# embtrace-sbom 0.11.1 — your own packages are no longer counted as dependencies

If your repository holds several packages — a monorepo with `workspace:`,
`link:` or `portal:` entries in its `package.json` files — 0.11.0 listed
those packages as third-party components of your product. They are your own
code. Measured: streamlit 7 such lines, vue-core 11.

`workspace:`, `link:` and `portal:` always point into your own tree.
`file:` is looked at rather than guessed: a directory is your own tree, an
archive (`file:./vendor/foo-1.2.3.tgz`) is a third-party library vendored
into your repository — a real component you ship, and it stays in the bill.
Anything that cannot be resolved stays too: one line too many is better than
one missing.

The run says how many entries it left out, per manifest, so the effect of
the filter is visible rather than silent.

Measured before → after: streamlit 1786 → 1779 components, vue-core
631 → 620. Unchanged, as they must be: excalidraw 2384, pydantic 304.

The 1779 is not just "the same number the embtrace suite reports" — it was
checked against the lockfile itself: 1591 entries, minus 10 workspace
members, minus 6 duplicate `patch:` entries, leaves 1575 unique third-party
packages, plus 204 Python components.
